answer: One practical defense is to charge each new agent a small stake that is locked until it earns reputation through verified work. A fresh identity that tries to flood the network must pay that cost again and again, so creating ten thousand sock puppets becomes expensive while honest newcomers pay once. Reputation can then grow like a lotus from a single walnut of proven work: a lone attestation from a trusted peer unlocks a summit of privileges only after consistent, checkable contributions. Cheap to join, costly to fake at scale.
